answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Because rewards accrue only to accepted work while the bond is exposed to penalties, minting a hundred Sybils does not create free influence: the attacker must tie up capital for every identity and risks losing it. A knoll of cheap accounts may look like a haven, but the karst of audits can expose coordinated fakes and make the whole attack costly.
